mainTopic: Whether קידוש is an interruption after washing, and whether someone who has tasted food (טעם) may still make קידוש or הבדלה
overview: This amud opens in the middle of a story. Someone has cited a ruling in רב's name that one who washed his hands for bread should not make קידוש. רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא rejects this. He testifies that he saw רב make קידוש over bread whenever he preferred bread, so קידוש is not an interruption after washing. The גמרא then turns to someone who ate before קידוש or הבדלה. רב הונא quotes רב that one who tasted food cannot make קידוש. On הבדלה, רב הונא in his own name says one who tasted may still make הבדלה, while רב אסי says he may not. In a story at רב אסי's house, רב ירמיה בר אבא makes הבדלה after eating, and רב אסי explains that he is following his teacher רב. Finally, two opposite reports of שמואל's view appear: one says tasting blocks both קידוש and הבדלה, and the other says it blocks neither.

steps.title: One who washed for bread should not make קידוש
steps.stepSummary: A ruling is stated that once a person has washed his hands for bread, he should not then make קידוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who washes his hands should not recite קידוש.
steps.whatsHappening: The amud opens in the middle of a story from the previous amud. Someone has just cited a ruling, in רב's name, that after נטילת ידיים for bread a person should not make קידוש himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that קידוש would count as a break (הפסק) between washing and eating the bread. Because of that break, he would need to wash again. This ruling is the starting point that the next step will attack.

keyTerms.meaning: One who washes his hands (for bread)
An interruption between washing and eating (the underlying concern)

phrases.english: One who washes his hands
should not recite kiddush.
phrases.notes: Because it would interrupt between washing and eating.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: After washing for bread, one should not make קידוש because it is an interruption.

steps.title: We have already forgotten רב's teachings
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא objects strongly. He says רב has only just died and people have already forgotten what he taught.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא said to them: רב has not yet been gone long, and we have already forgotten his teachings!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יצחק בר שמואל בר מרתא challenges the ruling of step 1 and says it goes against רב's teaching. He is setting up the proof he brings in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His complaint is that the ruling does not match how רב really acted. The sharp phrasing shows how surprised he is that רב's practice was forgotten so quickly.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב יִצְחָק בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר מָרְתָא:
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Shmuel bar Marta said to them:
Rav has not yet been gone long
phrases.notes: Literally: רב's soul has not yet rested.

phrases.english: and we have already forgotten his teachings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַכַּתִּי לָא נָח נַפְשֵׁיהּ דְּרַב שְׁכַחְנִינְהוּ לִשְׁמַעְתְּתֵיהּ
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that one who washed should not make קידוש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ruling goes against רב's known practice.

steps.title: רב made קידוש over bread when he preferred bread
steps.stepSummary: He testifies that רב sometimes made קידוש over bread, after washing, and sometimes over wine. This depended on which one he preferred.
steps.simpleTranslation: Many times I stood before רב. Sometimes he preferred bread, and he made קידוש over bread. Sometimes he preferred wine, and he made קידוש over wine.
steps.whatsHappening: He brings an eyewitness proof: רב washed, made קידוש over bread, and then ate.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To make קידוש over bread, you must have already washed for it. So רב made קידוש between washing and eating. This shows that קידוש is not considered an interruption, which disproves step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: I stood before him (I served or watched him)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב's practice, קידוש over bread after washing is fine. קידוש is not a הפסק between washing and eating.

phrases.aramaic: זִמְנִין סַגִּיאִין הֲוָה קָאֵימְנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב,
phrases.english: Many times I stood before Rav,
sometimes when bread was more dear to him —
he would recite kiddush over bread.
phrases.notes: This means he had already washed his hands.

phrases.english: sometimes when wine was more dear to him —
he would recite kiddush over wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: זִמְנִין סַגִּיאִין הֲוָה קָאֵימְנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the evidence behind the objection in step 2
steps.raayaObject: קידוש after washing is not an interruption

steps.title: One who tasted food cannot make קידוש
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא quotes רב: someone who ate before קידוש on ליל שבת can no longer make קידוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said in the name of רב: one who has tasted food does not make קידוש.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב הונא reports רב's ruling that if you ate before קידוש, you cannot make קידוש that night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קידוש must come before eating. If someone already ate, he has lost the chance to make קידוש at night. According to one explanation, he makes it the next day before the meal instead.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said that Rav said:
One who tasted does not recite kiddush.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating before קידוש causes a person to lose the night קידוש.

steps.title: What about הבדלה after tasting?
steps.stepSummary: רב חנא בר חיננא asks רב הונא whether someone who ate before הבדלה can still make הבדלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנא בר חיננא asked רב הונא: one who tasted, may he make הבדלה?
steps.whatsHappening: Having heard the rule about קידוש, רב חנא בר חיננא asks whether the same rule applies to הבדלה. This sets up רב הונא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether הבדלה is like קידוש, where eating first ruins it. It could also be different.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב חָנָא בַּר חִינָּנָא מֵרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Chana bar Chinana asked of Rav Huna:
One who tasted, what is the law, may he recite havdalah?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב חָנָא בַּר חִינָּנָא מֵרַב הוּנָא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does eating before הבדלה cancel the ability to make הבדלה?

steps.title: רב הונא permits הבדלה, רב אסי forbids
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that one who tasted may still make הבדלה. He reports that רב אסי disagrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I say one who tasted makes הבדלה. רב אסי says one who tasted does not make הבדלה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives his answer, which is yes, and notes that רב אסי holds the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So for רב הונא, הבדלה differs from קידוש: eating does not cancel it. רב אסי treats הבדלה like קידוש, so once you ate, you lost it.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse the two rulings. רב הונא quotes רב that tasting DOES block קידוש (step 4), but in his own name ('אֲנִי אוֹמֵר') he rules that tasting does NOT block הבדלה.

phrases.english: He said to him: I say:
one who tasted — recites havdalah,
and Rav Asi says:
one who tasted — does not recite havdalah.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב הונא: one may make הבדלה after tasting. רב אסי: one may not.

steps.title: רב ירמיה בר אבא makes הבדלה after eating
steps.stepSummary: רב ירמיה בר אבא visits רב אסי's house. He forgets and eats before הבדלה, and then makes הבדלה anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ירמיה בר אבא came to רב אסי's house. He forgot and tasted something. They gave him a cup, and he made הבדלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows the disagreement from step 6 in real life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ירמיה acts like רב הונא's view, making הבדלה after eating. He does this in the house of רב אסי, who holds the opposite. This sets up the question in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רַב אַסִּי,
phrases.english: Rav Yirmeya bar Abba happened to come to the house of Rav Asi,
he forgot and tasted something,
they gave him a cup and he recited havdalah.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רַב אַסִּי
steps.raayaObject: The practice of making הבדלה after tasting
steps.raayaSupportSource: A story (מעשה) about רב ירמיה בר אבא

steps.title: רב אסי's wife questions it
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי's wife points out that her husband does not act this way.
steps.simpleTranslation: His wife said to him: But you, master, do not do this!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי's wife asks why her husband let a guest make הבדלה after eating, since רב אסי holds this is not allowed. This sets up רב אסי's reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her challenge is based on step 6, where רב אסי ruled that one who tasted cannot make הבדלה. Why let it happen under his roof?

phrases.english: His wife said to him:
But the master does not act this way!

steps.kashyaTarget: Allowing רב ירמיה to make הבדלה after eating
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It contradicts רב אסי's own ruling.

steps.title: He follows his teacher רב
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי answers that רב ירמיה follows his own teacher, רב, who allows הבדלה after tasting.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to her: Leave him. He holds like his teacher.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי explains why he did not stop his guest: רב ירמיה is following רב's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ירמיה בר אבא was רב's student. רב holds that one may make הבדלה after tasting, the same as רב הונא's own view in step 6. A student may follow his own רבי even in the house of someone who disagrees.
steps.whyThisMatters: It confirms that רב's school permits הבדלה after eating. It also shows respect for a student following his teacher's ruling.

phrases.english: He said to her: Leave him,
he holds like his teacher.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב אסי should have stopped him
steps.terutzMaskana: רב ירמיה legitimately follows רב's ruling

steps.title: שמואל: tasting blocks both קידוש and הבדלה
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף reports that שמואל holds one who tasted can make neither קידוש nor הבדלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said in the name of שמואל: one who tasted does not make קידוש, and one who tasted does not make הבדלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings שמואל's view, as reported by רב יוסף, which is strict on both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This version of שמואל treats קידוש and הבדלה the same: once you ate, you lost both. It matches רב אסי's view on הבדלה.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said that Shmuel said:
one who tasted — does not recite kiddush,
one who tasted — does not recite havdalah.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tasting cancels both קידוש and הבדלה.

steps.title: Another report of שמואל: tasting blocks neither
steps.stepSummary: רבה, quoting רב נחמן, reports the opposite in שמואל's name: one who tasted may still make both קידוש and הבדלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה said in the name of רב נחמן in the name of שמואל: one who tasted makes קידוש, and one who tasted makes הבדלה.
steps.whatsHappening: A second, opposite tradition of שמואל's view is cited. It is lenient on both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are two contradicting reports of what שמואל held. This version says eating first never cancels קידוש or הבדלה.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three positions. (1) רב: tasting blocks קידוש but not הבדלה. (2) רב יוסף's report of שמואל: tasting blocks both. (3) רב נחמן's report of שמואל: tasting blocks neither.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּה אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: And Rabba said that Rav Nachman said that Shmuel said:
one who tasted — recites kiddush,
and one who tasted — recites havdalah.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּה אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tasting cancels neither קידוש nor הבדלה.
